advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Strip trailing inline comments (and handle unmatched trailing content) in parse_manifest_paths before tokenizing the RHS.
evidence: scripts/check_deploy_manifest.py:86-94: after stripping a single leading/trailing quote, `for token in rhs.split(): ... tokens.add(token)` — a trailing `# note` becomes tokens '#' and 'note'.
Current autodeploy.sh manifest lines (e.g. :172, :190, :233) have no trailing inline comments, so this is latent, not active.
advisory.finding: parse_manifest_paths does not strip trailing inline comments after the closing quote of a *_PATHS= assignment. If a manifest line is written as `FOO_PATHS='a b'  # note`, the '#' and 'note' tokens are parsed as path tokens (the trailing-quote strip only removes one quote at rhs[-1], and split() then yields the comment words), silently corrupting the manifest token set.
scenarios: A future edit adds an inline comment on a *_PATHS= line; bogus tokens '#'/comment words enter the coverage set and could spuriously 'cover' a derived path via is_covered prefix matching.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Either drop the unused argv parameter from main() or document why it is intentionally accepted-and-ignored.
evidence: scripts/check_deploy_manifest.py:240: `def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:` — argv is never referenced in the body (:241-256).
Test calls `gate.main([])` (tests/unit/test_check_deploy_manifest.py) relying on the parameter existing but passing an empty list.
advisory.finding: main() declares an argv parameter but never uses it; the entrypoint and test both call it, but argv is dead. This is a minor maintainability wart that can mislead a reader into thinking CLI args are honored.
scenarios: A reader assumes passing argv changes behavior; it silently does nothing.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a unit test driving _derive_from_compose with a tmp docker-compose.yml containing an active `entrypoint:`/`command:` directive referencing a .sh, asserting the resolved path and source label.
evidence: scripts/check_deploy_manifest.py:153-165 _derive_from_compose parses `entrypoint:`/`command:` lines and resolves .sh tokens
search of infra/compose/docker-compose.yml for `entrypoint:` returned `(no matches)`; all `.sh` occurrences are in comment lines

ABSENCE: no test in test_check_deploy_manifest.py builds a docker-compose.yml with an active `entrypoint: /app/...sh` or `command:` directive; _make_repo only creates scripts and only _resolve_repo_script is unit-tested
advisory.finding: _derive_from_compose (the compose entrypoint/command derivation source) is never exercised: the real infra/compose/docker-compose.yml has no active `entrypoint:`/`command:` line referencing a `.sh` (all matches are comments), and no unit test constructs a compose file with such a directive. The regex-match, comment-skip, `split(':',1)` label, and resolution logic could all be broken while every test stays green — leaving one of the gate's two derivation sources unverified.
scenarios: A refactor breaks the `entrypoint|command` regex or the `stripped.split(':',1)[1]` value extraction; the gate silently derives nothing from compose and the test suite stays green
A future service adds an entrypoint script in docker-compose.yml that never lands in a *_PATHS manifest — the derivation source meant to catch it is itself unverified
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a tmp-repo test: write infra/compose/docker-compose.yml with `entrypoint: /app/infra/scripts/foo.sh` plus infra/scripts/foo.sh, then assert derive_paths(root) contains 'infra/scripts/foo.sh' with a 'docker-compose.yml:entrypoint' source.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that drives check()/main() to a non-empty-diagnostics state and asserts a non-zero exit (return 1).
evidence: scripts/check_deploy_manifest.py:240-249 main() prints diagnostics and `return 1` when check() is non-empty
tests/unit/test_check_deploy_manifest.py:56 `assert gate.main([]) == 0` — only the clean/return-0 path is asserted
ABSENCE: no test invokes main against a repo_root where check() returns diagnostics to assert the return-1 (gate-fails) behavior
advisory.finding: main()'s failure branch (the `::error::` message, per-diagnostic print loop, fix hint, and `return 1`) is never exercised — only `gate.main([]) == 0` is asserted. The non-zero exit code that `make lint` relies on to gate a drifting tree is untested, so a regression making main() return 0 (or crash) on non-empty diagnostics would not be caught.
scenarios: A repo with an EXCLUSIONS entry naming a missing file (check() returns a 'stale' diagnostic) — main() must return 1; a regression returning 0 lets make lint pass over a rejected tree
A refactor to main() that swallows diagnostics or mis-returns the exit code
advisory.suggested_fix: Since main() is hardcoded to REPO_ROOT, either parametrize main(repo_root=...) or monkeypatch gate.REPO_ROOT/EXCLUSIONS to a state producing diagnostics and assert the return value is 1.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Make _resolve_repo_script emit a diagnostic (or fail) on an ambiguous (>1 match) container-absolute basename instead of silently returning None, so an unresolvable-but-present script is flagged rather than dropped.
evidence: scripts/check_deploy_manifest.py:118-123: `matches = sorted(... repo_root.glob("infra/**/" + Path(raw).name) ...); return matches[0] if len(matches) == 1 else None`

Docstring at :115-117 asserts a generated-in-image script 'resolves to nothing and is correctly skipped' — but the same silent-None also fires for a genuine ambiguous/unresolvable basename, making a possibly deploy-relevant script INVISIBLE to the coverage check.

Litmus: the derivation produces 'nothing for this reference' both when the script is truly image-generated AND when a real script's basename is ambiguous — the two are indistinguishable, so an omission cannot be told from a clean skip.
dropped.finding: _resolve_repo_script returns None (silently discarding the reference) when a container-absolute basename matches zero or more-than-one files under infra/**. A deploy-relevant script whose basename collides across infra/** — or a reference the parser cannot resolve — is silently dropped from the derived set, so it is never cross-checked against the manifests. The gate then reports 'covered' for a path it never actually examined, which is the fail-open drift class the gate exists to prevent.
scenarios: Two infra/** subtrees each contain a script of the same basename that a Dockerfile ENTRYPOINT names by absolute path — neither is derived, so a later drift to either goes uncaught.
